artifact.canonical_name: Efficient Integration of cross platform functions onto service-oriented architectures

sources.title: Efficient Integration of cross platform functions onto service-oriented architectures
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose hardware- and middleware-agnostic application development with standardized interfaces and machine-readable application/middleware descriptions to reduce repeated integration work across heterogeneous automotive software platforms.
An example application is integrated onto both AUTOSAR Adaptive and ROS 2 using semi-automated tooling, demonstrating applicability of the cross-platform concept.

limitations.text: The accessible primary abstract states that efficiency metrics are presented but does not expose their definitions, baseline, numerical values, toolchain effort, or experimental conditions.

A single example integration does not establish general integration cost or portability across arbitrary AUTOSAR vendor stacks, Classic/Adaptive releases, ROS 2 distributions, or production E/E programs.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Efficient Integration of cross platform functions onto service-oriented architectures; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies the platform-agnostic/interface/machine-readable integration concept and an AUTOSAR Adaptive/ROS 2 demonstration, but the stated efficiency metrics are not visible in the accessible primary text.

unresolved_questions: Inspect the full paper's integration-efficiency metrics, baseline/manual workflow, toolchain and example-application setup before quantitative use.

editorial.why_now_note: Platform heterogeneity is a direct software-integration consequence of consolidating functions onto HPCs while retaining AUTOSAR Classic, Adaptive and ROS 2 ecosystems.
editorial.rationale: Highly relevant concept, but quantitative integration-efficiency claims should not enter the report until the full metric definitions and baselines are verified.
